JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioners in the nutshell is that, on 13.03.2022 at about 9.30 a.m, the deceased in order to attend the marriage function he was proceeding his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-08-Q-786 on the extreme left side of Malur - Tekal road slowly and cautiously by observing all the traffic rules and regulations, while so proceeding and reached near Bhuvanahalli Gate, Malur Taluk, Kolar District, at that time suddenly the Tractor and Trailer bearing Reg.No.KA-08-T-6801 and KA-08-T- 6802 which was driven by its driver on opposite direction i.e,
from Tekal towards Malur side came in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger the human life and dashed the deceased's motorcycle.
Due to the terrific impact the deceased sustained grievous injuries all over his body.
Immediately after the accident he was rushed to Silicon City Hospital, Hosakote wherein first aid was provided to him.
For further management he was shifted to Hosmat Hospital, Bengaluru and thereafter to Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru.
Despite best efforts put in by the duty doctors the deceased succumbed to the injuries on 15.03.2022 at about 2.45 p.m.
Postmortem
was conducted and corpse was handed over to the family members, who conducted funeral and other ceremonies by spending substantial amount.
The accident was caused due to the sole negligence of driver of Tractor and Trailer.
The respondents No.1 and 2 being the owner and insurer thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1.
Respondent No.1 appeared through his counsel, he failed to contest the matter by filing the written statement.
4. The respondent No.2 filed objections statement admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Tractor and Trailer bearing Reg.No.KA-08-T-6801 and KA-08-T-6802.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.
Non -compliance of section, 56, 66, 147, 149, 134(c), 158(6) of IMV Act is pleaded.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Negligence on the part of the driver of its insured tractor and trailer is denied by this respondent.

Per contra it is alleged that the deceased who was riding the motorcycle without having a proper lookout at the vehicular movement on the public place and the deceased was solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident.
In fact deceased was also not wearing helmet and also not possessing valid DL at the time of alleged accident

. Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL and further the said insured vehicle did not holding valid and effective Permit and FC.

Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its Geetha vs Thimmaiah on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130408262/
3 possession to such a driver.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further contended that the petitioners are called upon to prove their relationship and dependency with the deceased.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners proves that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased ?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 13.03.2022 at about 9.30 a.m,
near Bhuvanahalli Gate, Malur - Tekal Road, Malur Taluk, Kolar District, due to actionable negligence of the driver of Tractor &
Trailer bearing Reg.No.KA-08-T-6801 & KA-08-T- 6802 ?

3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed? If so, at what rate and from whom ?
4) What order or award ?
6. The Petitioner No.4 examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's .
P1 to 5 and Ex.P.16 to 25 were marked on behalf of the petitioners.
Further the petitioners have examined the petitioner No.6 as PW.2 and through her Ex.P.6 to 15 were marked.
The petitioners have also examined the employer of deceased i.e., Assistant Accountant, Divisional Office, KSRTC, Kolar Division as PW.3 and got marked Ex.P.26 document.
In order to prove the defence, the respondent No.2 did not choose lead evidence.
7. Arguments were addressed on both sides.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.
The counsel for respondent No.2 filed written arguments.

8. My answers to the above issues are as follows:-
 Issue No.1 : Partly In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final order  for the following :
 REASONS  9. ISSUE NO.2: The occurrence of the accident on the Geetha vs Thimmaiah on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130408262/
4
relevant date, time and place is not in dispute.
The parties are also not at variance with regard to the factum of the death of the deceased due to the injuries sustained in the said accident.
The conflict is with respect to actionable negligence.
The petitioners plead that the accident was caused due to the sole negligence of the driver of offending Tractor and trailer.
Whereas the Insurance Company contends that the accident in question occurred because of negligence of the deceased.
10. Mr.Srirangappa - the father of deceased set the criminal law into the motion by lodging Ex.P.2-First information statement.

Based on the said FIS, the jurisdictional police registered FIR as per Ex.P.1, investigated the matter and laid charge sheet (Ex.P.3) against the driver of the Tractor and Trailer for the offences punishable u/s's 279, 304(A) of IPC.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Though the respondent No.2 has denied the cause of the accident, they have not let in any cogent evidence to prove their defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioners.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of tractor & trailer.
11. Further the learned counsel for the Insurance Company argued that as the deceased was riding the motorcycle without wearing helmet, contributory negligence must be attributed to him.

The mere fact that at the time of accident the petitioner was not wearing helmet, may not, by itself,
without anything more, make him guilty of contributory negligence.
At the most, he can held be guilty of being a party to the violation of law.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Civil Appeal No.79/2020 (Mohammad Siddique & another V/s National Insurance Company Ltd & others), wherein it is held that 'Simply because there is a violation of Section 129 of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 by a victim in an accident, there is no presumption that there is contributory negligence on the part of the person who was not wearing the helmet'.

sentences.text: Added to this in a claim for compensation u/s 166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimants have to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656.

sentences.text:
With this observation, issue No.2 is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
12. ISSUE NO.1:

The petitioners claim that, petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 and 3 are the minor children, petitioner No.4 & 5 are parents, petitioners No.6 to 8 are the married sisters and petitioner No.9 is the elder brother of the deceased.
To prove the same, petitioner No.4 filed affidavit in lieu of his chief-examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The Aadhar cards and ration card of petitioner No.1 to 4 are marked at Ex's.P.16 to 20 and contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.
Further the PW.1 has also produced Ex.P.21 being the death certificate of petitioner No.5 who is none other than the mother of the deceased.
On perusal of Ex.P.21 it is clear that during the pendency of the petition the mother of the deceased / PW.4 died on 09.12.2022.
It is vociferously contended by respondent No.2 that petitioners No.6 to 9 are not dependents of the deceased as such they are not entitled for any claim under the dependent head.

Geetha vs Thimmaiah on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130408262/
5 13.
It is well settled that dependency must be established in order to claim compensation.
However during the course of his cross-examination PW.1 admitted that he was retired police head constable and was getting pension of Rs.25,000/- p.m.
He further admitted that in the ration card there is only shown the names of his son, daughter in law and their children.
Further he admitted that petitioners No.6 to 8 are married and are residing at their husband's house.
Further he admitted that petitioner No.9 was unemployed and he was married.
Further when its comes to the dependency of the petitioner No.9, it is relevant to note that the petitioner No.9 is the brother of the deceased.
Petitioner No.9 has attained majority.

Added more there is nothing placed on record before the court that the petitoner No.9 was the dependent of the earning of the deceased when such being the case he cannot be considered as a dependent on the deceased.
In this view of matter petitioners No.6 to 9 cannot be said to be dependents on the earnings of their deceased brother.
Under such circumstances only the petitioners No.1 to 4 are entitled for compensation under the head 'Loss of dependency'.
Hence, this Tribunal answers to issue No.1 Partly In the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3 :
14. LOSS OF DEPENDENCY INCLUDING FUTURE PROSPECTS:
The petitioners have not produced any age proof documents.

But the documents available on record i.e., Aadhar card,
Lerner's Licence and ID card issued by KSRTC the date of birth of deceased is shown as 12.08.1980,
which indicates that he was aged 41 years 7 months 1 days on the date of accident.

Therefore the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group is '14'.
15.

In order to substantiate the fact the deceased was working as a driver-cum-conductor at KSRTC,
Kolar Depot, Kolar, the petitioners have produced salary slip at Ex.P.5 and also got examined the Assistant Accountant, Divisional Office, KSRTC, Kolar Division as PW.3.
This witness produced the certified copy of pay slip of the deceased, which is exhibited at ExP.26.
The testimony of this witness which is fortified by the said exhibit was not displaced during cross-examination.
16. Generally it is the last drawn salary that needs to be taken into consideration for the calculation of compensation.

But in this case as the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident that occurred on 13.03.2022, as per Ex.P.26 his income for March-2022 cannot be considered for determining compensation.
Further during March-2022, the deceased's pay was calculated for 13 days only as he was absent from work from 14 to 31 during that month.
Hence his salary for the last full worked month i.e., February- 2022 is taken into account for computing the dependency compensation.
The gross salary of the deceased for the said month is Rs.37,176.23.
On careful perusal of the salary slip it includes the over duty charge.
It is needless to note that on every month any person could not possible to do over duty.
The over duty charges be changes month to month.
It is depending on over duty made by the employee.
Therefore, the over duty charges cannot be considered as monthly fixed income.
As such the gross salary of deceased is considered as Rs.37,176.23 - 9,392.63) Rs.27,784/-.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited v/s Pranay Sethi and others, except income tax no deduction is to be made from the salary of the deceased qua other allowances.

Even otherwise from the elicitation brought out during the course of cross-examination of PW.3 it is crystal clear that they have been given death benefits of Rs.1,00,000/- as DRBF and Rs.3,00,000/- as KSRTC Geetha vs Thimmaiah on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130408262/
6
General Insurance.
17. Be that as it may, annual income works out to Rs.3,33,408/- (Rs.27,784 X 12).
Out of the said annual income, professional tax and income tax needs to be deducted.
The calculation table for which stands as follows :

Annual Gross Salary 3,33,408  (Rs.27,784 x12)
 Annual Professional Tax (less) 2,400  Total 3,31,008  Less Tax Exemption 2,50,000  (for the year 2022)
 Taxable Income 81,008  Tax payable @ 5% on 4,050  Rs.81,008/- (during the year  2022)

Gross Income 3,33,408  Less Total Tax payable 6,450  (2,400 + 4,050 =12,086)
 Annual Established Income 3,26,958  Monthly Established Income 27,247  (3,26,958 / 12)
18.
In the case on hand the deceased was aged 41 years.
His income is taken as Rs.27,247/- p.m.
In this case the deceased being an employee of the State Government had a permanent job.
Therefore as per dictum of Hon'ble Apex Court in AIR 2017 SC 5157, 30% of income is to be added towards future prospects.
30% of Rs.27,247/- works out to Rs.8,174/-.
Therefore the total income comes to Rs.35,421/- (27,247 + 8,174).
There are four dependents.
Hence 1/4th is to be deducted towards his personal expenses.
1/4 th of Rs.35,421/- works out to Rs.8,855/-.
Income for consideration is Rs.26,566/- (35,421 - 8,855).
Annual income works out to Rs.3,18,792/- (26,566 X 12).
Appropriate multiplier is '14'.
Thus loss of dependency works out to Rs.44,63,088/- (Rs.3,18,792 X 14) which is rounded off to Rs.44,63,000/-.

19. Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

Hence this Tribunal award Rs.18,150/- towards loss to estate and Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years.

Rs.48,400/- towards consortium to the petitioner No.1 by applying the observations made in the aforesaid case, as more than 6 years elapsed from the date of order amount of consortium, funeral expense and loss of estate to be enhanced.

20. In this case, the petitioner No.2 & 3 are the children and the petitioner No.4 is the father of the Geetha vs Thimmaiah on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130408262/
7 deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of a children and father as the case may be.

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of a father cause great shock and agony to the children of the deceased and she lost her love and affection towards his/her father, as well as Petitioner no.4 towards deceased his son.
Therefore, petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.
21. MEDICAL EXPENSES :
Medical bills produced by PW.2 are marked at Ex.P6.
As per that, the claimants have spent Rs.10,05,875/- towards medical expenses of the deceased.
The petitioners have made wrong calculation of medical bills.
Further on calculation of Ex.P.6 of bills No.1 to 25 the total amount comes to Rs.9,15,439/-.
On perusal of SL.No.13 & 15 are the advance receipts of Hosmat Hospital and Sl.No.21 to 24 are the advance receipts of Manipal Hospital.
Hence they are not considered.
Hence excluding the same the petitioners are entitled to Rs.6,60,439/- (Rs.9,15,439 - Rs.2,55,000) which is rounded off to Rs.6,60,500/- is awarded under this head.

22. The calculation table stands as follows :
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1. Towards loss of dependency Rs.44,63,000/-
 2. Towards loss of Consortium to Rs. 48,400/-
 the petitioner No.1  3. Towards loss to estate Rs. 18,150/-
 4. Towards transportation of dead Rs. 18,150/-
 body funeral and obsequies  ceremony expenses  5. Towards loss of Filial consortium Rs. 1,20,000/-

6 . Medical Expenses incurred by the Rs. 6,60,500/-
 deceased during the tenure of his  treatment before his death  Total Rs.53,28,200/-
23. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
24. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the Tractor and trailer bearing Reg.No.KA-08-T-6801 and KA-08-T-6802 are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a.
Geetha vs Thimmaiah on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130408262/
8 from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Hence issue No.3 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
25. ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.53,28,200/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 60% Petitioner No.2 - 15% Petitioner No.3 - 15% Petitioner No.4 - 10% Petitioner No.5 - Died - Petitioner No.6 - Nil - Petitioner No.7 - Nil - Petitioner No.8 - Nil - Petitioner No.9 - Nil - Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 a sum equal to 25% shall be deposited in her names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to her through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner No.1 is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time.

The share amount apportioned in the name of minor petitioners No.2 & 3 is ordered to be deposited in their names vide Fixed Deposit till they attain the age of majority,
at any Nationalized/Scheduled Bank as per the choice of the next friend/Natural guardian of the said minor petitioners.

After deposit of compensation amount the office is directed to release the entire share with interest to the petitioner No.4 through NEFT/RTGS by way of E- payment on Geetha vs Thimmaiah on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130408262/

proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a Road Traffic accident.
The accident was caused due to the sole negligence of driver of Tractor and Trailer.
Non -compliance of section, 56, 66, 147, 149, 134(c), 158(6) of IMV Act is pleaded.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
opennyai_summary.issue:
5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners proves that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased ?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 13.03.2022 at about 9.30 a.m,
near Bhuvanahalli Gate, Malur - Tekal Road, Malur Taluk, Kolar District, due to actionable negligence of the driver of Tractor &
Trailer bearing Reg.No.KA-08-T-6801 & KA-08-T- 6802 ?
3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed? If so, at what rate and from whom ?
4) What order or award ?
The parties are also not at variance with regard to the factum of the death of the deceased due to the injuries sustained in the said accident.
opennyai_summary.arguments: The petitioners plead that the accident was caused due to the sole negligence of the driver of offending Tractor and trailer.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Based on the said FIS, the jurisdictional police registered FIR as per Ex.P.1, investigated the matter and laid charge sheet (Ex.P.3) against the driver of the Tractor and Trailer for the offences punishable u/s's 279, 304(A) of IPC.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Though the respondent No.2 has denied the cause of the accident, they have not let in any cogent evidence to prove their defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioners.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of tractor & trailer.
It is vociferously contended by respondent No.2 that petitioners No.6 to 9 are not dependents of the deceased as such they are not entitled for any claim under the dependent head.
It is well settled that dependency must be established in order to claim compensation.
Petitioner No.9 has attained majority.
Added more there is nothing placed on record before the court that the petitoner No.9 was the dependent of the earning of the deceased when such being the case he cannot be considered as a dependent on the deceased.
In this view of matter petitioners No.6 to 9 cannot be said to be dependents on the earnings of their deceased brother.
Under such circumstances only the petitioners No.1 to 4 are entitled for compensation under the head 'Loss of dependency'.
But in this case as the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident that occurred on 13.03.2022, as per Ex.P.26 his income for March-2022 cannot be considered for determining compensation.
On careful perusal of the salary slip it includes the over duty charge.
It is needless to note that on every month any person could not possible to do over duty.
The over duty charges be changes month to month.
It is depending on over duty made by the employee.
Therefore, the over duty charges cannot be considered as monthly fixed income.
As such the gross salary of deceased is considered as Rs.37,176.23 - 9,392.63) Rs.27,784/-.
As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited v/s Pranay Sethi and others, except income tax no deduction is to be made from the salary of the deceased qua other allowances.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Hence this Tribunal award Rs.18,150/- towards loss to estate and Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the Tractor and trailer bearing Reg.No.KA-08-T-6801 and KA-08-T-6802 are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a.

25. ISSUE NO.4 :
In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.53,28,200/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 60% Petitioner No.2 - 15% Petitioner No.3 - 15% Petitioner No.4 - 10% Petitioner No.5 - Died - Petitioner No.6 - Nil - Petitioner No.7 - Nil - Petitioner No.8 - Nil - Petitioner No.9 - Nil - Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 a sum equal to 25% shall be deposited in her names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to her through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner No.1 is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time.
The share amount apportioned in the name of minor petitioners No.2 & 3 is ordered to be deposited in their names vide Fixed Deposit till they attain the age of majority,
at any Nationalized/Scheduled Bank as per the choice of the next friend/Natural guardian of the said minor petitioners.
